sources.entry: Featbit - Enterprise-grade feature flag platform that you can self-host. (Source Code) MIT Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: FeatBit is a self-hostable feature flag platform for gradual rollouts, impact monitoring, and quick rollbacks of features.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes FeatBit as a feature flag platform for rolling out features gradually, monitoring their technical and business impact, and rolling back problematic features. Setup is covered via a Docker Compose launch (clone the repo at tag 6.1.0, then run docker compose up -d) that opens a web portal with default demo credentials. Developers connect an official SDK using an environment SDK key and connection URLs, then evaluate flags by key in code; the example uses the .NET SDK with a boolean flag. The README lists self-hosting routes for Kubernetes (Helm charts or manifests), AWS and Azure Container Apps (Terraform projects), Microsoft Aspire, and Docker Compose. It also notes a hosted FeatBit Cloud option. The project is described as Open Core: most code is MIT-licensed, but some features require a valid license key.
use_cases: gradually roll out new features to users
feature flag and toggle management for developers
self-host a feature flag service on Kubernetes
A/B style testing of features with business metrics
how_to_run: Open the portal in a browser and sign in with the default credentials (test@featbit.com / 123456)
Connect an official SDK using your environment's SDK key and connection URLs
For Kubernetes, AWS, Azure Container Apps, or Microsoft Aspire, follow the linked self-hosting guides
notable: Self-host options covering Docker Compose, Kubernetes, AWS, Azure Container Apps, and Microsoft Aspire
Gradual percentage-style rollout with the ability to switch a flag off instantly
Hosted FeatBit Cloud available as an alternative to self-hosting
caveats: Open Core: certain features require a valid license key
Default demo credentials are published in the README and must be changed for real use
Quick start requires Git and Docker with Docker Compose
summary.license: MIT (most of the code; certain features require a license key)
keywords: roll out features to a small group
turn features on and off without deploying
